claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a transition material between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms.
Lattice distortion contributes to CoCrFeMnNi's proposed ability to mediate the creep-mechanism transition.
Grain-boundary segregation contributes to CoCrFeMnNi's proposed ability to mediate the creep-mechanism transition.
Dislocation density contributes to CoCrFeMnNi's proposed ability to mediate the creep-mechanism transition.
The proposed initial material is polycrystalline CoCrFeMnNi with an average grain size of 100 nm.
The proposed loading condition is a uniaxial tensile stress of 100 MPa at 800 K.
The proposed test environment is vacuum at 10^-5 Pa.
Grain-boundary dislocation networks are the structural mediator of the proposed creep transition.
The operative creep mechanism is thermally activated dislocation glide and climb.
Grain-boundary-engineered CoCrFeMnNi is predicted to have a 20% higher creep strain rate than CoCrFeMnNi without grain-boundary engineering.
A creep-rate increase of at least 10% is sufficient to confirm a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Grain-boundary engineering may introduce additional defects that affect creep behavior.
The hypothesis is falsified if the engineered material's creep strain rate is less than 10% above the baseline.
An absolute creep-rate threshold of 1.1 x 10^-6 s^-1 represents a 10% increase over baseline.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies only tensile stress and temperature, whereas the mediator and outcome depend on grain-boundary engineering; no grain-boundary-engineering intervention is defined.
The absolute threshold of 1.1 x 10^-6 s^-1 implicitly assumes a baseline of 1.0 x 10^-6 s^-1, but no absolute baseline creep rate is stated.
